title: Staff console: queues, people, approvals and logs
summary: The clinic verification queue (Phase 12). References show the details to check grouped under plain labels, a short checklist where each item has its own state, and a status said in words on every row. The screens follow the licence review already shipped, so staff learn one pattern. References 04 and 06 to 16 (2026-11-21) prepare the rest of the console: finding a person and signing them out everywhere, the bar shown while acting as someone else, notes only staff see, a request that waits for a second person, a log of who did what, and failed deliveries that can be sent again. References 17 to 22 (2026-11-22) prepare two small slices: queues with pages (12.6: a count in words, Previous and Next, the page kept in the address) and the sign-in-again message (12.7: said when the page opens, with a button, and nothing typed is lost).

references.pattern: What was sent, grouped under plain labels, each value on its own line
references.why: 'Review and submit' lists the business details in small cards: a quiet label, then the value, with the website as a link that opens in a new tab.
references.apply: Show the filing as label and value pairs (legal name, NIF, billing address, website); numbers in a monospace face; the register links right under the value they check.
references.query: back office review page to approve or reject a business verification request with checklist and reason

references.pattern: A short checklist where every item is one sentence and the action stays off until all pass
references.why: 'Review submission' is a list of requirements, each one sentence with its own state, and Submit stays disabled until every item passes; a line above says what happens after submitting.
references.apply: Two checks as full sentences; Approve stays disabled until both are ticked; one line says what to do to approve.
references.query: back office review page to approve or reject a business verification request with checklist and reason

references.pattern: Status in words on every row, and who has to act
references.why: 'Verify details' lists each request with its state in words (Verifying, Verified, Requires action), so it is clear which ones wait on the reader.
references.apply: Queue states say who acts next: 'To check' (staff) and 'Waiting on the clinic'; decided filings read 'Verified' or 'Rejected'.
references.query: back office review page to approve or reject a business verification request with checklist and reason

references.pattern: People list with the account state in words on every row
references.why: 'People' is a table of name, email and status. The status reads 'Active', 'Suspended' or 'Waiting to be confirmed' in words, with a 'Guest' tag where it applies. A search by name or email and a status filter sit above the table.
references.apply: The staff Users list: name, email, role and state in words (Active, Suspended, Email not confirmed), with a search by name or email and a state filter. Colour only supports the word.
references.query: users table in an admin dashboard with account status and a ban or suspend action

references.pattern: Sessions table with one button above it to sign out everywhere else
references.why: 'Active sessions' lists device, location, IP, started on and last used, with a menu on each row and one red button above the table: 'Log out everywhere else'.
references.apply: Put 'Sign out everywhere' above the user's sessions table. Confirm it with the number of sessions it will end and ask for a reason, since staff do this on someone else's account.
references.query: admin console user detail page with active sessions and suspend user action

references.pattern: User detail with a short action list beside the identity: impersonate, change password, ban, delete
references.why: A user's page puts the avatar, email, last sign-in and user id on the left with four actions under them: Impersonate user, Change password, then Ban user and Delete user in red. Verified email and phone sit in cards on the right.
references.apply: Keep account actions in one short list beside the user's identity, everyday ones first and Suspend set apart. 'View as this person' opens a dialog that asks for a reason before it starts; Clerk starts without one, Eleva asks.
references.query: admin logging in as a user to view their account

references.pattern: A full-width bar while acting as someone: who you are acting as, and the way out on the same bar
references.why: After 'Act as a user' is chosen from a menu, a blue bar spans the top of the view: 'You're acting as' with the person's email in a selector, and 'Exit mode' with a close icon on the right. The view below is framed in the same colour for as long as the mode is on.
references.apply: While staff view Eleva as a member or an expert, keep a bar on every page: 'Viewing as {name}' and 'Stop viewing'. Say it in words and frame the page, so it never rests on colour alone, and show the time left when the session is limited.
references.query: admin logging in as a user to view their account

references.pattern: Staff-only comments in the customer's timeline, with the audience stated under the box
references.why: The customer page has a Timeline with a comment box on top and one line under it: 'Only you and other staff can see comments'. Staff comments and system events ('You sent a store credit issued email to this customer') share one dated list.
references.apply: Internal notes sit in the user's activity timeline with the line 'Only Eleva staff can see notes' under the box. Each note shows who wrote it and when; the member or expert never sees them.
references.query: customer profile with internal notes visible only to the team

references.pattern: Internal note composer that is labelled and looks different from a reply
references.why: On a contact's page the composer is labelled 'Internal note' on a tinted background, with the placeholder 'Add a note about this contact'. The activity list below can be narrowed by type and by person.
references.apply: Label the composer 'Internal note' and tint it, so staff never mistake it for a message to the person. Let staff narrow the timeline to notes only.
references.query: customer profile with internal notes visible only to the team

references.pattern: Approval panel: what is asked, by whom and when, a comment, then Reject and Approve
references.why: A spend request opens in a side panel: the title with the tag 'Pending your approval', 'Submitted by Sam Lee on 2025-11-27', the amount, who it is for and the category, then a comment box and attachments, with Reject and Approve at the bottom right. The list behind it has 'Pending your approval' and 'All requests in approval'.
references.apply: An action that needs two people opens the same way for the second person: what will happen, who asked, when and why, then 'Approve' and 'Reject', and a rejection needs a reason. The person who asked cannot approve her own request.
references.query: payment waiting for approval from a second team member with approve and reject buttons

references.pattern: The waiting state as a count: '0/1 Approved' on the row, in an Approve tab with its own number
references.why: 'Bills' has tabs for Draft, Approve, Ready for payment and Paid, each with a count. Rows under Approve show '0/1 Approved' as their status, with approve and reject icons at the end of the row.
references.apply: Give requests that wait for a second person their own tab with a count, and say on each row who asked and how many approvals it has and needs ('Waiting for 1 approval'). Use buttons with words where Acctual uses a bare tick and cross.
references.query: payment waiting for approval from a second team member with approve and reject buttons

references.pattern: Audit log with one filter per question: when, who, what was changed, which event
references.why: 'Audit log' shows 'Last updated just now' with Refresh, then filters for Date range, Updated by, Updated resources, Event and Belongs to, and an Export button. Each row has the date and time, the person, the resource and the event. A note beside the table says what the log is for.
references.apply: Eleva's audit viewer: filters for date, staff member, record and action above the table; rows with time, who, what and on which record; an export. One line on top says what is recorded.
references.query: audit log page with filters by actor, action and date

references.pattern: Each log line is a sentence, and it opens in place to show the detail
references.why: Rows read as sentences ('Sam Lee added sender identity "Sam Lee"') with the timestamp and time zone at the right. A row opens in place to a 'Log entry' with its fields. The filters above are date range, team member, IP address and event type, with Export CSV top right.
references.apply: Write each audit row as a sentence (who did what to which record) with the exact time and time zone. Open a row to show the reason given and what changed; never show a member's health details there.
references.query: audit log page with filters by actor, action and date

references.pattern: Webhook page: events on the left with a status in words, the chosen event on the right with Replay
references.why: The endpoint's page says what it listens for, its status and when it was created. 'Events' lists each delivery with its type, age and 'Success'. The selected one shows its id, timestamp, HTTP status code, number of attempts, response body and payload, with a 'Replay' button.
references.apply: Staff see webhook events as a list with provider, type, time and state in words. One event opens beside the list with its attempts, the last error and 'Run again'. Mask personal data in the payload.
references.query: webhook delivery attempts list with failed events and a resend button

references.pattern: Failed deliveries can be ticked and retried together
references.why: 'Deliveries' filters by channel, status and date range. Each row has the time, the message, the recipient and a 'Failed' tag. Ticking rows shows '4 selected', '4 failed emails selected' and a 'Retry selected' button. 'Last updated today at...' and an auto refresh switch sit above the list.
references.apply: Let staff narrow the list to failed events, tick several and press 'Run again' once. Say how many are selected and when the list was last refreshed, and report the result for each event.
references.query: webhook delivery attempts list with failed events and a resend button

references.pattern: Table footer in three parts: rows per page on the left, '1-6 of 6' and Previous / Next in words on the right
references.why: 'Visitors' ends with a footer row: a '25 rows per page' select on the left and, on the right, the range and the total ('1-6 of 6') beside 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons with words. On a single page both buttons are greyed out but stay in place, so the footer never jumps. Search, a filter and a sort sit above the table.
references.apply: Both staff queues end with the same footer: 'Showing 1 to 25 of 112' on the left, 'Previous' and 'Next' as words on the right. The page size is fixed at 25 to start; add the 'rows per page' select only when a queue regularly runs past a few pages. At the first and last page the button is disabled, not hidden.
references.query: admin table with pagination showing rows per page and a count of results

references.pattern: A review queue split by state, each tab with its count, and Prev / Next under the rows
references.why: 'Pull Requests' is a queue of requests waiting for a decision. Tabs on top read 'Pending (1)', 'Approved (0)', 'Rejected (0)'. Each row is a sentence ('Alex Smith wants to publish…'), when it was created, a status pill, and reject and approve at the end. The footer has 'Prev' and 'Next' on the left and the page size (10, 20, 30 rows) on the right.
references.apply: Say how much waits on the queue itself: 'Showing 1 to 25 of 112' now, and a count on each state ('To check (12)', 'Waiting on the clinic (4)') when states become tabs or a filter. Changing the state goes back to page 1. Use buttons with words where StackAI uses a bare tick and cross, and 'Previous' in full.
references.query: review queue list of pending requests with previous and next page buttons

references.pattern: Filters as chips above the table, and 'Showing 1-4 of 4' beside Previous / Next below it
references.why: A member's 'Logs' has filter chips on top ('Event: Invited to community, Removed from comm… + 8', 'Performed by', 'Date'), then a three-column table. Under it: 'Previous', 'Next' and 'Showing 1-4 of 4'. The count is of the filtered list, so the reader sees at once how much the filter left.
references.apply: Keep the page and any filter in the address (?page=2&state=pending), so Back, reload and a shared link open the same rows. The count is of the filtered list. When a filter leaves nothing, say so and offer 'Clear filter'; that is a different message from an empty queue.
references.query: activity log list with a load more button at the bottom

references.pattern: A small dialog over the page: one sentence on why, then the ways to sign in again as buttons
references.why: On account settings, a sensitive action opens 'Reauthenticate' over the page: 'You need to reauthenticate yourself to perform this sensitive action', then two full-width buttons, 'Password' and 'Email link'. The settings page stays behind the dialog, so nothing the person did is lost, and they choose the method that suits them.
references.apply: When a decision is refused because the sign-in is more than 12 hours old, say why in one sentence and give one button, 'Sign in again', beside the button that was pressed. The page stays as it is: the ticks and the typed reason are kept and come back after signing in. Use plain words where GitBook says 'reauthenticate'.
references.query: session expired message asking to sign in again

references.pattern: Signing in again in place: the account's email is already filled in, and every sign-in method is offered
references.why: 'Confirm your account' opens over Settings: one sentence, then 'Continue with Google', 'Continue with Facebook' and 'Continue with Apple', and below them the email already filled in with the line 'The email address associated with your current account', a password field, 'Log out' and 'Log in with email'. The person never retypes who they are.
references.apply: 'Sign in again' opens Eleva's sign-in with the staff member's email already filled in and comes back to the same review. Nothing is asked twice: the email, the ticks and the reason are all carried. Offer the same methods as the normal sign-in (Google, email link, password), so nobody has to remember or retype a password to go on. Todoist blames a failed check; Eleva gives the real reason.
references.query: session expired message asking to sign in again

references.pattern: A banner above the form says what is needed before submitting and why, with the action on the same line
references.why: 'Review your information' opens with an amber box above the details: 'Your email has not been confirmed. For security purposes, you will need to confirm your email before submitting your account verification.' and a 'Resend email' button at its right. The person learns it before reading and filling in the page, not after pressing Submit.
references.apply: When a review opens on a sign-in older than 12 hours, show a banner above 'Your decision': 'Sign in again before you decide', one sentence on why, and 'Sign in again'. The filing stays readable. Use an icon and words, never colour alone, and keep the tone calm: this is a routine check, not an error.
references.query: banner at the top of a page warning that you need to verify your identity before making changes

judging_criteria: In the queue, can staff see which filings wait on them and which wait on the clinic, oldest first, with the clinic and its legal name on the row? (Revolut Business 13-admin/03)
On a filing, is everything staff must compare (legal name, NIF, billing address, website, owner) on one screen, with the public register one click from the value it checks? (Stripe 13-admin/01)
Is approving impossible until both checks are confirmed, and are sending back and rejecting impossible without a reason the clinic can read? (Klaviyo 13-admin/02)
After a decision, does the page say what happened and what happens next, and does a refusal (already decided, new details, your own clinic) say what to do?

On a user's page, can staff see the account state in words and every active session, and sign out one device or all of them, or suspend the account, each with a confirmation that says what will happen? (1Password 13-admin/04, Homerun 13-admin/06)
Does 'View as' ask for a reason before it starts, and does a bar that names the person and offers 'Stop viewing' stay on every page while it lasts? (Clerk 13-admin/07, Base44 13-admin/08)

Is it clear at the composer that a note is for Eleva staff only, does each note show who wrote it and when, and is the note absent from everything the member, the expert or the clinic can open (their activity, exports and emails)? (Shopify 13-admin/09, Zendesk 13-admin/10)

For an action that needs two people, can the second person see what is asked, by whom, when and why, and approve or reject it, while the first sees that it is waiting and for how many approvals, and is the person who asked unable to approve their own request? (Airwallex 13-admin/11, Acctual 13-admin/12)

Can staff answer who did what, to which record and when from the audit log, by filtering on person, action, record and date, with each row readable as a sentence? (Front 13-admin/13, Customer.io 13-admin/14)

Can staff find the webhook events that failed, see why each one failed and how many times it was tried, run one or several again, and then see the result of each one, not only that a retry was asked? (Resend 13-admin/15, Customer.io 13-admin/16)

Does each queue load one page at a time, say where the reader is in words ('Showing 26 to 50 of 112'), move with 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons that are disabled at the ends, and keep the page in the address so Back, reload and a shared link open the same rows? (Navattic 13-admin/17, StackAI 13-admin/18, Circle 13-admin/19)

When a decision needs a newer sign-in, does the reviewer learn it when the page opens, before typing; does the message say why and offer 'Sign in again'; and are the ticks and the typed reason still there after signing in, with no detail asked twice? (GitBook 13-admin/20, Todoist 13-admin/21, Airwallex 13-admin/22)
